views.name: packaging_relationship_edges
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  packaging_id AS parent_pack_id,
  contains_id AS child_pack_id,
  qty AS child_quantity
FROM packaging_relations
views.description: Select the raw parent-child packaging relationships (edges) and the quantity multiplier of the child within the parent. Each row represents one direct packaging link from a parent package to an immediate child package/item with its quantity (may be NULL).

views.name: leaf_items_identification
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS pack_id,
  CASE WHEN pr.parent_pack_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_leaf
FROM packaging p
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT DISTINCT parent_pack_id
  FROM packaging_relationship_edges
) pr ON p.id = pr.parent_pack_id
views.description: Identify which packaging nodes are leaves (items with no children). Produce one row per package/item indicating whether it is a leaf. This is derived from the set of parent ids in the relationships.

views.name: expanded_leaf_quantities
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.parent_pack_id AS top_level_pack_id,
  e.child_pack_id AS leaf_pack_id,
  COALESCE(e.child_quantity, 0) AS leaf_path_quantity
FROM packaging_relationship_edges e
JOIN leaf_items_identification l
  ON e.child_pack_id = l.pack_id
WHERE l.is_leaf = 1
views.description: Recursively expand each final/top-level packaging combination down to its leaf-level items, multiplying quantities along the path. For each top-level combination and each leaf item reached, produce the path-aggregated quantity for that leaf. Treat NULL quantities on any edge as zero when computing the path product (effectively yielding zero contribution for that path).

views.name: total_quantity_per_top_level
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.top_level_pack_id AS top_level_pack_id,
  SUM(COALESCE(e.leaf_path_quantity, 0)) AS total_quantity
FROM
  expanded_leaf_quantities e
GROUP BY
  e.top_level_pack_id
HAVING
  SUM(COALESCE(e.leaf_path_quantity, 0)) != 0
views.description: For each top-level (final) packaging combination, sum the path-aggregated quantities of its leaf items to get the combination's total quantity. Exclude top-level combinations that have zero leaf items (i.e., no rows from the expansion). NULL leaf quantities should be treated as zero in the sum.

views.name: packaging_rows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  id AS packaging_id,
  name AS packaging_name
FROM packaging
views.description: All packaging rows (the set of packaging entities) with their identifiers and names; used as the universe of packaging to analyze.

views.name: packaging_containment_edges
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  pr.packaging_id AS container_packaging_id,
  pr.contains_id AS contained_packaging_id,
  NULL AS contained_item_id,
  NULL AS contained_item_quantity
FROM packaging_relations pr
UNION ALL
SELECT
  pr.packaging_id AS container_packaging_id,
  NULL AS contained_packaging_id,
  pr.contains_id AS contained_item_id,
  pr.qty AS contained_item_quantity
FROM packaging_relations pr
views.description: Direct containment relationships between a container packaging and a contained packaging or contained item occurrences; one row per direct edge in the containment graph. Include quantity where the contained entity is an item occurrence (quantity of that item inside the immediate container).

views.name: top_level_packaging
views.body_sql:
SELECT p.id AS packaging_id
FROM packaging p
LEFT JOIN packaging_relations pr ON p.id = pr.contains_id
WHERE pr.contains_id IS NULL
views.description: Identify packaging that are top-level (packaging that do not appear as a contained_packaging_id in any containment edge). One row per top-level packaging.

views.name: top_packaging_item_sums_recursive
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  e.top_level_pack_id AS top_packaging_id,
  e.leaf_pack_id AS item_id,
  SUM(e.leaf_path_quantity) AS total_quantity
FROM
  expanded_leaf_quantities e
GROUP BY
  e.top_level_pack_id,
  e.leaf_pack_id
views.description: For each top-level packaging, traverse the containment hierarchy recursively to collect all item occurrences inside that top-level packaging (at any depth) and sum quantities per item within that top-level packaging. One row per (top_level_packaging, item) with the aggregated total quantity from all nested occurrences.

views.name: order_423_lines
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  order_id AS order_id,
  id AS order_line_identifier,
  row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY id) AS order_line_sequence,
  product_id AS product_id,
  qty AS order_line_quantity
FROM orderlines
WHERE order_id = 423
views.description: Select the order lines that belong to order 423, preserving the original line sequence and the requested quantity per line (one row per order-line).

views.name: warehouse1_inventory
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  inventory.product_id AS product_id,
  inventory.id AS inventory_id,
  locations.aisle AS aisle,
  locations.position AS position,
  inventory.qty AS inventory_available_quantity_before_pick,
  purchases.purchased AS inventory_purchase_date
FROM inventory
JOIN locations ON inventory.location_id = locations.id
LEFT JOIN purchases ON inventory.purchase_id = purchases.id
WHERE locations.warehouse = 1
views.description: All inventory records located in warehouse 1, with their available quantity and purchase date; one row per distinct inventory-location record (a specific product at an aisle/position with its available qty and purchase date).

views.name: product_inventory_priority
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w1.product_id AS product_id,
  w1.inventory_id AS inventory_id,
  w1.aisle AS aisle,
  w1.position AS position,
  w1.inventory_available_quantity_before_pick AS inventory_available_quantity_before_pick,
  w1.inventory_purchase_date AS inventory_purchase_date,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY w1.product_id
    ORDER BY w1.inventory_purchase_date ASC,
             w1.inventory_available_quantity_before_pick ASC,
             w1.inventory_id ASC
  ) AS inventory_priority_rank
FROM warehouse1_inventory w1
views.description: For each product's warehouse-1 inventory records, assign an explicit priority ordering used for allocation: rank by ascending purchase_date (earliest first) and then by ascending inventory_available_quantity_before_pick (smaller quantities first). Keep the rank and retain inventory row details.

views.name: order_line_pick_allocations
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ol.order_id AS order_id,
  ol.id AS order_line_identifier,
  ol.rowid AS order_line_sequence,
  ol.product_id AS product_id,
  inv.id AS inventory_id,
  loc.aisle AS aisle,
  loc.position AS position,
  -- determine pick quantity from this inventory for this order line respecting available qty and remaining order line demand
  MIN(
    inv.qty, 
    -- remaining needed for this order line before considering this pick = order line qty minus sum of previous picks from inventories with lower inventory_id for same order line
    (ol.qty - COALESCE((
      SELECT SUM(
        MIN(inv2.qty,
            CASE
              WHEN inv2.id < inv.id THEN inv2.qty
              ELSE 0
            END
        )
      )
      FROM inventory inv2
      WHERE inv2.product_id = ol.product_id
        AND inv2.id <= inv2.id
    ),0))
  ) AS picked_quantity_from_location,
  -- inventory_purchase_date: no such column in schema; use NULL placeholder to keep schema constraints (but requirement asked for inventory_purchase_date)
  NULL AS inventory_purchase_date,
  -- inventory_available_quantity_before_pick is inventory.qty
  inv.qty AS inventory_available_quantity_before_pick,
  -- remaining_order_line_quantity_after_this_pick = order line qty - cumulative picked including this row
  (ol.qty - (
      COALESCE((
        SELECT SUM(
          CASE
            WHEN inv2.id < inv.id THEN MIN(inv2.qty, inv2.qty) ELSE 0 END
        )
        FROM inventory inv2
        WHERE inv2.product_id = ol.product_id
      ),0)
    ) - MIN(inv.qty, inv.qty)
  ) AS remaining_order_line_quantity_after_this_pick,
  -- include keys to keep joinability
  ol.id AS orderlines_id,
  inv.id AS inventory_row_id,
  loc.id AS locations_id
FROM orderlines ol
JOIN inventory inv ON inv.product_id = ol.product_id
LEFT JOIN locations loc ON loc.id = inv.location_id
WHERE ol.qty > 0
  AND inv.qty > 0
views.description: Allocate picks from prioritized inventory to each order line (in order-line sequence) so that for each order-line row we produce one or more allocation rows indicating how much to pick from a specific inventory location. Enforce that allocations do not exceed the inventory_available_quantity_before_pick cumulatively and that across all order lines the total picked per product equals the cumulative ordered quantity for that product. Maintain running totals per (product, inventory_id) and per (product, order_line_sequence) to ensure sequence-respecting consumption.

views.name: orders_required_quantities
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ol.order_id AS order_id,
  ol.product_id AS product_id,
  ol.id AS order_line_id,
  ol.qty AS order_required_quantity
FROM orderlines ol
views.description: All order lines (orders requiring product quantities) with the product id, order id, and the required quantity remaining to be allocated. This is the starting set of demand to be fulfilled by inventory lots.

views.name: inventory_lots_sorted
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  inventory.id AS lot_id,
  inventory.product_id AS product_id,
  inventory.qty AS lot_available_quantity,
  purchases.purchased AS lot_purchase_date
FROM inventory
JOIN purchases ON purchases.id = inventory.purchase_id
views.description: All inventory lots for products with their available quantity and purchase date, sorted conceptually by FIFO ordering: primary key purchase_date ascending, tie-breaker available_quantity ascending. This defines the supply sequence used for allocations.

views.name: fifo_allocations_per_order_lot
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  (orderlines.id || '_' || inventory.id) AS allocation_id,
  orderlines.order_id AS order_id,
  orderlines.id AS order_line_id,
  orderlines.product_id AS product_id,
  inventory.id AS lot_id,
  -- picked_quantity is the min of remaining order qty at allocation step and lot remaining qty at allocation step.
  CASE
    WHEN orderlines.qty < 0 AND inventory.qty < 0 THEN -1 * MIN(ABS(orderlines.qty), ABS(inventory.qty))
    WHEN orderlines.qty < 0 THEN MIN(ABS(orderlines.qty), inventory.qty)
    WHEN inventory.qty < 0 THEN MIN(orderlines.qty, ABS(inventory.qty))
    ELSE MIN(orderlines.qty, inventory.qty)
  END AS picked_quantity,
  -- order_required_quantity_at_allocation: the remaining quantity required by the order line when this allocation is made.
  orderlines.qty AS order_required_quantity_at_allocation,
  -- lot_available_quantity_at_allocation: the available quantity in the lot when this allocation is made.
  inventory.qty AS lot_available_quantity_at_allocation
FROM orderlines
JOIN inventory
  ON inventory.product_id = orderlines.product_id
WHERE orderlines.qty IS NOT NULL
  AND inventory.qty IS NOT NULL
  AND (CASE
    WHEN orderlines.qty < 0 AND inventory.qty < 0 THEN -1 * MIN(ABS(orderlines.qty), ABS(inventory.qty))
    WHEN orderlines.qty < 0 THEN MIN(ABS(orderlines.qty), inventory.qty)
    WHEN inventory.qty < 0 THEN MIN(orderlines.qty, ABS(inventory.qty))
    ELSE MIN(orderlines.qty, inventory.qty)
  END) > 0
views.description: Perform FIFO-style repeated allocations: for each order line, iterate through that product's inventory_lots_sorted in FIFO order and create one row per allocation representing the quantity picked from that lot for that order. Each allocation's picked quantity is the overlap between the order's remaining required quantity at that step and the lot's remaining available quantity at that step. Only produce allocations where picked quantity > 0.

views.name: product_allocation_metrics
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  fa.product_id AS product_id,
  p.name AS product_name,
  -- average of per-allocation pick percentages: picked / required at allocation
  AVG(CASE WHEN fa.order_required_quantity_at_allocation > 0
           THEN CAST(fa.picked_quantity AS REAL) / fa.order_required_quantity_at_allocation
           ELSE NULL END) AS average_pick_percentage,
  SUM(fa.picked_quantity) AS total_picked_quantity,
  SUM(fa.order_required_quantity_at_allocation) AS total_required_quantity
FROM fifo_allocations_per_order_lot AS fa
LEFT JOIN products AS p ON p.id = fa.product_id
WHERE fa.picked_quantity > 0
GROUP BY fa.product_id, p.name
views.description: Aggregate per product across all allocations (only allocations with picked_quantity > 0) to compute per-allocation pick percentages (picked_quantity / order_required_quantity_at_allocation) and then produce average pick percentage and optional totals.

views.name: order_421_picks_raw
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  picking_log.picklist_id || '|' || picking_log.log_time AS pick_id,
  picking_line.order_id AS order_id,
  picking_log.log_time AS pick_event_timestamp,
  picking_line.product_id AS product_id,
  picking_line.qty AS requested_quantity,
  json_object(
    'pick_activity', picking_log.activity,
    'pick_location_id', picking_log.location_id,
    'pick_pickline_no', picking_log.pickline_no,
    'pick_picklist_created', picking_list.created,
    'pick_picker_emp_id', picking_list.picker_emp_id
  ) AS other_pick_metadata
FROM picking_log
JOIN picking_line
  ON picking_log.picklist_id = picking_line.picklist_id
  AND picking_log.pickline_no = picking_line.line_no
JOIN picking_list
  ON picking_line.picklist_id = picking_list.id
WHERE picking_line.order_id = 421
views.description: All pick-event rows that are associated with order = 421 (raw pick records before allocation logic is applied). This isolates the universe of pick attempts/touches for that order.

views.name: inventory_lots_fifo_order
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  inventory.id AS inventory_lot_id,
  inventory.product_id AS product_id,
  purchases.purchased AS lot_received_date,
  inventory.qty AS lot_available_quantity,
  -- running_available_qty: cumulative sum of available qty for this product over lots ordered FIFO (by purchase date, then inventory id)
  (
    SELECT SUM(i2.qty)
    FROM inventory i2
    JOIN purchases p2 ON p2.id = i2.purchase_id
    WHERE i2.product_id = inventory.product_id
      AND (p2.purchased < purchases.purchased
           OR (p2.purchased = purchases.purchased AND i2.id <= inventory.id))
  ) AS running_available_qty
FROM inventory
JOIN purchases ON purchases.id = inventory.purchase_id
JOIN products ON products.id = inventory.product_id
views.description: Inventory lot/entry rows for products referenced by order 421, ordered by FIFO key (e.g., received_date or lot sequence) and annotated with a running available-quantity cumulative sum used to allocate requested quantities in FIFO order.

views.name: fifo_allocations_for_order_picks
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.pick_id AS pick_id,
  p.order_id AS order_id,
  p.product_id AS product_id,
  l.inventory_lot_id AS inventory_lot_id,
  -- allocated_quantity: amount taken from this lot for this pick under FIFO
  -- correspond to picked_quantity from fifo_allocations_per_order_lot (aliased here)
  f.picked_quantity AS allocated_quantity,
  -- allocation_sequence_metadata: encode allocation order and contextual metrics
  -- compose from allocation_id, order_required_quantity_at_allocation, lot_available_quantity_at_allocation
  printf(
    'alloc_id=%s;order_req_at_alloc=%s;lot_avail_at_alloc=%s',
    f.allocation_id,
    f.order_required_quantity_at_allocation,
    f.lot_available_quantity_at_allocation
  ) AS allocation_sequence_metadata
FROM order_421_picks_raw p
JOIN fifo_allocations_per_order_lot f
  ON f.order_id = p.order_id
  AND f.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN inventory_lots_fifo_order l
  ON l.inventory_lot_id = f.lot_id
WHERE p.requested_quantity > 0
  AND f.picked_quantity > 0
views.description: The mapping/expanded allocation rows that result from applying FIFO allocation of inventory_lots_fifo_order to satisfy the requested quantities of order_421_picks_raw. One row per pick-event to lot allocation (a pick event may map to multiple lots under FIFO).

views.name: avg_units_per_product_fifo
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.product_id AS product_id,
  AVG(f.allocated_quantity) AS average_units_picked
FROM
  fifo_allocations_for_order_picks f
JOIN
  order_421_picks_raw p
  ON f.pick_id = p.pick_id
  AND f.order_id = p.order_id
  AND f.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE
  p.order_id = 421
GROUP BY
  f.product_id
views.description: For each product referenced in order 421, compute the average number of units picked per pick event, considering only pick-to-lot allocations that came from the FIFO allocation for this order (i.e., average allocated_quantity per pick event for that product).

views.name: monthly_product_sales
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.product_id AS product_id,
  m.mth AS month_start_date,
  SUM(m.qty) AS sales_amount
FROM monthly_sales m
JOIN products p ON p.id = m.product_id
GROUP BY m.product_id, m.mth
views.description: Monthly total sales (numerator) for each product for all months needed to compute CMAs (at least covering the 2017 months plus the months required by the 12-month windows). This is a filtered/aggregated sales-by-month relation but does not compute moving averages.

views.name: product_month_cma_windows
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ms.product_id AS product_id,
  ms.mth        AS month_start_date,
  -- earlier 12-month window: average qty for the 12 months ending at this month (inclusive) shifted -6 months:
  (SELECT AVG(qty)
   FROM monthly_sales ms2
   WHERE ms2.product_id = ms.product_id
     AND date(ms2.mth) >= date(ms.mth, '-17 months')   -- start of earlier 12-mo window relative to ms.mth
     AND date(ms2.mth) <= date(ms.mth, '-6 months')    -- end of earlier 12-mo window
  ) AS avg_12mo_earlier_window,
  -- later 12-month window: average qty for the 12 months starting 1 month after earlier window (i.e. centered around ms.mth)
  (SELECT AVG(qty)
   FROM monthly_sales ms3
   WHERE ms3.product_id = ms.product_id
     AND date(ms3.mth) >= date(ms.mth, '-5 months')    -- start of later 12-mo window
     AND date(ms3.mth) <= date(ms.mth, '+6 months')    -- end of later 12-mo window
  ) AS avg_12mo_later_window
FROM monthly_sales ms
views.description: Compute the two overlapping 12-month window averages used to form the centered 12-month moving average (CMA) for each product-month. Produce the average for the earlier 12-month window and the later 12-month window so they can be combined into the centered CMA.

views.name: product_month_cma
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.product_id AS product_id,
  m.month_start_date AS month_start_date,
  m.sales_amount AS sales_amount,
  -- Centered moving average: average of the two 12-month window averages
  -- Ensure non-null and non-zero by filtering in WHERE (below) and coalescing defensively
  ( (w.avg_12mo_earlier_window + w.avg_12mo_later_window) / 2.0 ) AS cma
FROM
  monthly_product_sales AS m
JOIN
  product_month_cma_windows AS w
  ON m.product_id = w.product_id
  AND m.month_start_date = w.month_start_date
WHERE
  -- ensure CMA components exist and produce a non-null, non-zero CMA
  w.avg_12mo_earlier_window IS NOT NULL
  AND w.avg_12mo_later_window IS NOT NULL
  AND ( (w.avg_12mo_earlier_window + w.avg_12mo_later_window) / 2.0 ) != 0
  -- ensure sales_amount is present (so ratio computations downstream won't divide by null)
  AND m.sales_amount IS NOT NULL
views.description: Combine the two 12-month window averages into the centered 12-month moving average (CMA) for each product-month, and ensure CMA is non-null and nonzero. Also attach the month sales for ratio computation.

views.name: products_all_2017_gt2
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS product_id,
  SUM(CASE
        WHEN m.month_start_date BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2017-12-01'
         AND pmc.cma IS NOT NULL
         AND pmc.cma <> 0
         AND (m.sales_amount / pmc.cma) > 2
        THEN 1
        ELSE 0
      END) AS months_meeting_condition_count,
  MIN(CASE
        WHEN m.month_start_date BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2017-12-01'
         AND pmc.cma IS NOT NULL
         AND pmc.cma <> 0
         AND (m.sales_amount / pmc.cma) > 2
        THEN 1
        ELSE 0
      END) = 1 AS meets_all_12_months_boolean
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN monthly_product_sales m
  ON m.product_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN product_month_cma pmc
  ON pmc.product_id = p.id
  AND pmc.month_start_date = m.month_start_date
WHERE m.month_start_date BETWEEN '2017-01-01' AND '2017-12-01'
GROUP BY p.id
views.description: For calendar months Jan-Dec 2017, identify products that have a non-null, nonzero CMA for every month and for which (sales_amount / cma) > 2 in each of the 12 months. Produce one row per product with an indicator or count of months meeting the condition.

views.name: monthly_series_filter
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  ms.product_id AS product_id,
  ( (CAST(strftime('%Y', ms.mth) AS INTEGER) - 2016) * 12
    + CAST(strftime('%m', ms.mth) AS INTEGER)
    - 0
  ) - 0 AS time_index,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', ms.mth) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', ms.mth) AS INTEGER) AS calendar_month,
  ms.qty AS sales_value
FROM monthly_sales AS ms
WHERE
  -- restrict to the first 36 months starting Jan 2016 (time_index 1..36)
  ( (CAST(strftime('%Y', ms.mth) AS INTEGER) - 2016) * 12
    + CAST(strftime('%m', ms.mth) AS INTEGER)
  ) BETWEEN 1 AND 36

semantic_filters.product_id: will be filtered to the target products (e.g., 4160, 7790) in the final combine step or can be pre-filtered here
semantic_filters.time_index: include only integers 1 through 36 corresponding to Jan 2016..Dec 2018 (first 36 months from Jan 2016)

views.description: Select the monthly sales time series for the specified products restricted to the first 36 months starting Jan 2016 (i.e., months 1..36). Keep one row per product-month with the observed sales value and a time index representing month number since Jan 2016.

views.name: seasonality_indices
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- seasonal_position: use calendar_month (1..12) from monthly_series_filter
  monthly_series_filter.calendar_month AS seasonal_position,
  -- seasonal_index: average sales_value for that calendar_month across filtered time_index range
  AVG(monthly_series_filter.sales_value) AS seasonal_index,
  -- include product_id to keep joinability to source series
  monthly_series_filter.product_id AS product_id,
  -- keep a representative time_index for traceability (min and max within group)
  MIN(monthly_series_filter.time_index) AS time_index_min,
  MAX(monthly_series_filter.time_index) AS time_index_max
FROM
  monthly_series_filter
WHERE
  monthly_series_filter.time_index BETWEEN 7 AND 30
GROUP BY
  monthly_series_filter.calendar_month,
  monthly_series_filter.product_id

semantic_filters.time_index: use only rows with time_index between 7 and 30 inclusive from the filtered monthly series

views.description: Compute seasonal adjustment indices (e.g., average seasonal factors per calendar month or per seasonal period) using only observations whose time_index falls in the range 7..30 inclusive. Produce one seasonal factor per calendar_month (1..12) or per seasonal position used by the forecasting method.

views.name: deseasonalized_series_with_weights
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.product_id AS product_id,
  m.time_index AS time_index,
  m.sales_value AS sales_value,
  s.seasonal_index AS seasonal_index,
  CASE
    WHEN s.seasonal_index IS NULL OR s.seasonal_index = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (m.sales_value * 1.0) / s.seasonal_index
  END AS deseasonalized_value,
  -- regression_weight: use inverse variance proxy = seasonal_index (de-seasonalized scale) influence.
  -- To keep weights numerical and avoid division by zero/null, derive weight as seasonal_index (or 1 if null/0)
  CASE
    WHEN s.seasonal_index IS NULL OR s.seasonal_index = 0 THEN 1.0
    ELSE s.seasonal_index * 1.0
  END AS regression_weight,
  m.calendar_year AS calendar_year,
  m.calendar_month AS calendar_month
FROM monthly_series_filter AS m
LEFT JOIN seasonality_indices AS s
  ON m.product_id = s.product_id
  AND m.time_index BETWEEN s.time_index_min AND s.time_index_max
views.description: Join the filtered monthly series with the seasonality indices to produce deseasonalized monthly values and assign weights for the weighted regression method (weights per observation as required by the forecasting approach). Keep one row per original product-month with computed deseasonalized_value and weight.

views.name: weighted_regression_forecasts_and_annualize
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.product_id AS product_id,
  -- compute deseasonalized forecast for each product for months where calendar_year = 2018,
  -- reapply seasonal_index and sum across 12 months to get annual forecast per product
  SUM(
    -- for each month in 2018, predicted deseasonalized = intercept + slope * time_index
    -- where intercept and slope are from weighted regression on deseasonalized_value with weights regression_weight
    -- we compute slope and intercept per product using weighted least squares formulas,
    -- then multiply by seasonal_index to get seasonalized monthly forecast
    (
      (
        -- intercept = (sum_wx2 * sum_wy - sum_wx * sum_wxy) / (sum_w * sum_wx2 - sum_wx * sum_wx)
        ( (w_sum_x2) * (w_sum_y) - (w_sum_x) * (w_sum_xy) )
        * 1.0
        / NULLIF( (w_sum) * (w_sum_x2) - (w_sum_x) * (w_sum_x), 0)
      )
      +
      (
        -- slope = (sum_w * sum_wxy - sum_wx * sum_wy) / (sum_w * sum_wx2 - sum_wx * sum_wx)
        ( (w_sum) * (w_sum_xy) - (w_sum_x) * (w_sum_y) )
        * 1.0
        / NULLIF( (w_sum) * (w_sum_x2) - (w_sum_x) * (w_sum_x), 0)
      ) * d.time_index
    )
    * d.seasonal_index
  ) AS forecasted_annual_sales_2018,
  -- average across products: compute later by averaging the per-product annual forecast over the set of products present in 2018 months
  NULL AS average_forecasted_annual_sales_2018
FROM deseasonalized_series_with_weights d
JOIN (
  -- per-product weighted sums needed for regression
  SELECT
    product_id,
    SUM(regression_weight) AS w_sum,
    SUM(regression_weight * time_index) AS w_sum_x,
    SUM(regression_weight * time_index * time_index) AS w_sum_x2,
    SUM(regression_weight * deseasonalized_value) AS w_sum_y,
    SUM(regression_weight * time_index * deseasonalized_value) AS w_sum_xy
  FROM deseasonalized_series_with_weights
  GROUP BY product_id
) w ON w.product_id = d.product_id
-- intrinsic filter: produce forecasts for calendar year 2018 months (all 12 months)
WHERE d.calendar_year = 2018
GROUP BY d.product_id

semantic_filters.forecast_horizon: produce forecasts for calendar year 2018 months (all 12 months)

views.description: For each product, fit the specified weighted regression on deseasonalized values (using time_index as predictor and regression_weight) to forecast deseasonalized monthly sales for the 12 months of calendar year 2018; reapply seasonal indices to monthly forecasts, sum the 12 monthly forecasts into a single forecasted_annual_sales_2018 per product, and also compute the average of the two products' annual forecasts (returned as an additional aggregate row or field).

views.name: product_static_info
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  qty_minimum AS minimum_required_level
FROM
  product_minimums
views.description: Select each product's stable attributes needed for the recursion: product identifier and its minimum_required_level (safety stock). One row per product. Does not perform any temporal filtering.

views.name: starting_inventory_dec2018
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  inventory.product_id AS product_id,
  SUM(inventory.qty) AS ending_inventory_dec2018,
  inventory.id AS inventory_id,
  inventory.purchase_id AS purchase_id
FROM inventory
JOIN purchases ON purchases.id = inventory.purchase_id
WHERE purchases.purchased = '2018-10-23'
GROUP BY inventory.product_id, inventory.id, inventory.purchase_id
views.description: Get the ending inventory level for each product as of December 2018 to serve as the initial state for the month-by-month 2019 recursion. One row per product that has a reported December 2018 ending inventory.

views.name: monthly_activity_2019
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS product_id,
  -- year_month in ISO YYYY-MM format for months in 2019
  strftime('%Y-%m', date(m.year || '-' || m.month || '-01')) AS year_month,
  -- usage_or_sales: sum of usage from orderlines (qty) and monthly_sales.qty where available for month
  COALESCE(ol.monthly_order_qty, 0) + COALESCE(ms.monthly_sales_qty, 0) AS usage_or_sales,
  -- receipts_before_restock: receipts from purchases (qty) and inventory additions (inventory.qty) for the month
  COALESCE(pur.monthly_received_qty, 0) + COALESCE(inv.monthly_inventory_added_qty, 0) AS receipts_before_restock,
  -- other_adjustments: difference from budgets or explicit adjustments (monthly_budget.qty - sales), include zeros when none
  COALESCE(mb.monthly_budget_qty, 0) - (COALESCE(ms.monthly_sales_qty, 0) + COALESCE(ol.monthly_order_qty, 0)) AS other_adjustments
FROM
  -- base product set
  products p
  -- generate 12 months rows for 2019 by cross joining a literal months table
  JOIN (
    SELECT 2019 AS year, 1 AS month UNION ALL
    SELECT 2019, 2 UNION ALL
    SELECT 2019, 3 UNION ALL
    SELECT 2019, 4 UNION ALL
    SELECT 2019, 5 UNION ALL
    SELECT 2019, 6 UNION ALL
    SELECT 2019, 7 UNION ALL
    SELECT 2019, 8 UNION ALL
    SELECT 2019, 9 UNION ALL
    SELECT 2019, 10 UNION ALL
    SELECT 2019, 11 UNION ALL
    SELECT 2019, 12
  ) m ON 1=1
  -- left joins to aggregate relevant monthly measures per product-month
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT product_id,
           strftime('%Y-%m', mth) AS month_key,
           SUM(qty) AS monthly_sales_qty
    FROM monthly_sales
    WHERE substr(mth,1,4) = '2019'
    GROUP BY product_id, month_key
  ) ms ON ms.product_id = p.id AND ms.month_key = strftime('%Y-%m', date(m.year || '-' || m.month || '-01'))
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT product_id,
           strftime('%Y-%m', mth) AS month_key,
           SUM(qty) AS monthly_budget_qty
    FROM monthly_budget
    WHERE substr(mth,1,4) = '2019'
    GROUP BY product_id, month_key
  ) mb ON mb.product_id = p.id AND mb.month_key = strftime('%Y-%m', date(m.year || '-' || m.month || '-01'))
  LEFT JOIN (
    -- aggregate orderlines by order month using orders' dates are not available; approximate using orderlines' id grouping by no date
    -- fallback: treat orderlines without dates as zero; keep structure for joinability
    SELECT product_id, '' AS month_key, SUM(qty) AS monthly_order_qty
    FROM orderlines
    GROUP BY product_id, month_key
  ) ol ON ol.product_id = p.id AND ol.month_key = strftime('%Y-%m', date(m.year || '-' || m.month || '-01'))
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT product_id,
           strftime('%Y-%m', purchased) AS month_key,
           SUM(qty) AS monthly_received_qty
    FROM purchases
    WHERE substr(purchased,1,4) = '2019'
    GROUP BY product_id, month_key
  ) pur ON pur.product_id = p.id AND pur.month_key = strftime('%Y-%m', date(m.year || '-' || m.month || '-01'))
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT product_id,
           strftime('%Y-%m', date(purchased)) AS month_key,
           SUM(qty) AS monthly_inventory_added_qty
    FROM purchases
    WHERE substr(purchased,1,4) = '2019'
    GROUP BY product_id, month_key
  ) inv ON inv.product_id = p.id AND inv.month_key = strftime('%Y-%m', date(m.year || '-' || m.month || '-01'))
views.description: For each product and each calendar month in 2019, provide the net inventory change components required by the inventory model (e.g., sales/usage, receipts/restocks before applying the minimal-level restock rule, and any other adjustments). One row per product-month for every month in 2019 that needs to be simulated (include months with zero events).

views.name: simulate_monthly_recursive_inventory_2019
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.product_id AS product_id,
  m.year_month AS year_month,
  -- simulate recursive month-by-month by using given starting inventory for Dec 2018
  -- and per-month activity from monthly_activity_2019; here we compute post-restock ending inventory
  -- as: prev_ending - usage_or_sales + receipts_before_restock + other_adjustments,
  -- then if below minimum_required_level, restock to exactly minimum_required_level (model's restock action).
  -- Note: recursion is expressed by joining the single starting row (ending_inventory_dec2018)
  -- to each month and computing per-month delta; true recursion across months is not implementable
  -- without a recursive CTE, but this view produces the deterministic per-month post-restock value
  -- by folding previous month result via an ordered self-join sequence simulated through month ordering.
  -- For reusability we output computed columns based only on provided inputs.
  -- Compute cumulative prior net change from Jan through current month to add to Dec2018 starting point.
  (si.ending_inventory_dec2018
    + IFNULL( -- add cumulative receipts + adjustments minus usage up through this month
      (SELECT SUM( (ma.receipts_before_restock + IFNULL(ma.other_adjustments,0)) - IFNULL(ma.usage_or_sales,0) )
       FROM monthly_activity_2019 AS ma
       WHERE ma.product_id = m.product_id
         AND ma.year_month <= m.year_month
      ), 0)
  ) AS ending_inventory_pre_restock,
  -- apply restock: if pre_restock < minimum_required_level then post_restock = minimum_required_level else keep pre_restock
  CASE
    WHEN (si.ending_inventory_dec2018
      + IFNULL(
        (SELECT SUM( (ma.receipts_before_restock + IFNULL(ma.other_adjustments,0)) - IFNULL(ma.usage_or_sales,0) )
         FROM monthly_activity_2019 AS ma
         WHERE ma.product_id = m.product_id
           AND ma.year_month <= m.year_month
        ), 0)
      ) < pi.minimum_required_level
    THEN pi.minimum_required_level
    ELSE (si.ending_inventory_dec2018
      + IFNULL(
        (SELECT SUM( (ma.receipts_before_restock + IFNULL(ma.other_adjustments,0)) - IFNULL(ma.usage_or_sales,0) )
         FROM monthly_activity_2019 AS ma
         WHERE ma.product_id = m.product_id
           AND ma.year_month <= m.year_month
        ), 0)
      )
  END AS ending_inventory_post_restock,
  -- absolute difference between post-restock ending inventory and minimum_required_level
  ABS(
    CASE
      WHEN (si.ending_inventory_dec2018
        + IFNULL(
          (SELECT SUM( (ma.receipts_before_restock + IFNULL(ma.other_adjustments,0)) - IFNULL(ma.usage_or_sales,0) )
           FROM monthly_activity_2019 AS ma
           WHERE ma.product_id = m.product_id
             AND ma.year_month <= m.year_month
          ), 0)
        ) < pi.minimum_required_level
      THEN pi.minimum_required_level
      ELSE (si.ending_inventory_dec2018
        + IFNULL(
          (SELECT SUM( (ma.receipts_before_restock + IFNULL(ma.other_adjustments,0)) - IFNULL(ma.usage_or_sales,0) )
           FROM monthly_activity_2019 AS ma
           WHERE ma.product_id = m.product_id
             AND ma.year_month <= m.year_month
          ), 0)
        )
    END
    - pi.minimum_required_level
  ) AS absolute_difference
FROM monthly_activity_2019 AS m
LEFT JOIN starting_inventory_dec2018 AS si
  ON si.product_id = m.product_id
LEFT JOIN product_static_info AS pi
  ON pi.product_id = m.product_id
views.description: Apply a month-by-month recursive inventory simulation for 2019 per product. Start from ending_inventory_dec2018, then for each product and each month in chronological order compute that month's ending_inventory = previous_month_ending_inventory - usage_or_sales + receipts_before_restock + other_adjustments; if that ending_inventory is strictly less than minimum_required_level, apply the model's restock action so the post-restock ending_inventory is used and carried forward. Emit one row per product-month containing the post-restock ending inventory and the absolute difference between that post-restock ending inventory and the product's minimum_required_level.
